Honestly, compared to most course platforms, urlKajabihttps://www.kajabi.com/ is one of the easier ones to launch with if you are not super technical. It was basically built for coaches, consultants, creators, and business owners who want an “all in one” setup instead of piecing together 10 different tools. citeturn0search1turn0search4

For someone with your background in med spa consulting, Luxora systems, onboarding, trainings, and playbooks, you would probably pick it up pretty quickly because you already think in frameworks and client journeys.

Here’s the reality though:

### What’s easy about it
- Drag-and-drop course builder
- Upload videos/PDFs/modules easily
- Built-in landing pages
- Built-in checkout/payment processing
- Email automations included
- Membership/community options
- Pipelines/funnels already templated
- No coding required for most setups

Most people can get a basic course live in a weekend if their content already exists. citeturn0search4turn0search16turn0search18

### What actually takes time
The hard part is usually NOT the platform.

It’s:
- organizing content
- filming/editing videos
- structuring lessons
- creating workbooks/resources
- building sales messaging
- pricing
- launch strategy

Kajabi itself is relatively straightforward once you understand the dashboard.

### The learning curve
There *is* a learning curve if you want:
- advanced automations
- affiliate systems
- sophisticated funnels
- custom branding
- deeper analytics

A lot of reviews say beginners feel overwhelmed at first because Kajabi combines courses + website + email + funnels all in one place. citeturn0search4turn0search7

But once it “clicks,” people usually love having everything centralized.

### Biggest downside
Price.

Kajabi is premium-priced compared to alternatives like Teachable or Thinkific. Current plans are roughly in the $140–$200+/month range depending on features. citeturn0search2turn0search13

So it makes the most sense if:
- you are serious about monetizing
- you already have an audience/network
- you want branding + automations + CRM-style marketing
- you plan to scale courses/coaching/memberships

For your world specifically, I actually think Kajabi fits well because you already:
- run systems/processes
- have frameworks/playbooks
- do consulting
- have podcast content
- have educational IP for med spas
- likely need memberships and nurture automations

You could easily turn:
- Revenue Leak Audit
- front desk training
- memberships/packages training
- injector onboarding
- med spa profitability systems
- Luxora playbooks

…into structured Kajabi products.

If you want, I can also help you figure out:
- whether Kajabi is the BEST platform for your specific goals
- Kajabi vs GoHighLevel course hosting
- the easiest Luxora course structure
- how long it would realistically take you to build
- pricing strategy for med spa education
- what tech stack you actually need vs don’t need
